To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the capsid genes of two Sappori-like calicivirus (Hou/90 and Hou/86) were expressed in baculoviruses.

we expressed the capsid proteins of Sapporo like human calicivirues (Hou/90 and Hou/86) in insect cells using a baculovirus expression system, that these proteins self-assembled to form VLP, and that these VLPs are antigenic.
the capsid proteins of Sapporo like human calicivirues were produced and characterized in the baculovirus expression system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a baculovirus expression system for Sapporo-like capsid proteins.
the expression and characterization of SLCV capsid proteins in insect cell system.
the expression, characterization and antigenic properties of the capsid proteins of Sapporo calicivirues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the capsid proteins of Sapporo virus and other Sapporo-like viruses are expressed in insect cells by baculovirus vectors and can self-assemble to form virus-like particles (VPs) that can be purified and used for immunologic assays.
Sapporo-like viruses are a new species of calicivirus, distinct from other human calicivirus species.
the Sapporo virus is a member of a new group of caliciviridae, which is closely related to the group of Norwalk-like viruses, but which differs antigenically from them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully expressed capsid protein of Sapporo virus and developed an antigenic assay for detection of Sapporo viruses.
the Sapporo-like capsid protein is a useful antigen for serological detection of human calicivirus infection.
we have developed a system to express Sapporo-like capsid proteins in the baculovirus system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have been able to express the capsid protein from the Sapporo-like strains in insect cells and that the protein self-organizes into virus-like particles (Figure 1).
Sapporo-like viruses are antigenically distinct from Norwalk virus and other caliciviridae.
the Sapporo-like capsid proteins can be produced and characterized in a baculovirus expression system.
